newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, Cargill buying aids nearbys.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, Cargill buying aids nearbys.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mixed, and traders said steady buying by Cargill Investor Services helped boost the nearby contracts over the deferreds.

KCBT wheat also drew support from USDA, which reported export inspections of 14.3 million bushels of wheat during the week ended Jan 16. That was above the 12.1 million bushels reported during the previous week.
"Cargill's been a good buyer all day long. They've picked up around 10 million bushels between here and in Chicago," a KCBT trader said.
Some traders said they presumed Cargill's buying was commercially-related, but others declined to speculate.

Wheat also gained on talk that India may end up tendering for up to 200,000 tonnes of wheat. Earlier Tuesday, India's state-run State Trading Company announced a tender for 50,000 of wheat for arrival by the end of March.
KCBT wheat closed two cents lower to 5-1/2 cents higher, with March up 5-1/2 cents at $4.12-3/4 per bushel. May gained 3-3/4 cents to close at $3.76.
CIS bought 1.8 million March bushels and 600,000 July, traders said.

Wolcott Lincoln bought one million May and sold 1.3 million March and one million July. Prudential Securities bought 1.4 million May and E D & F Man International bought 1.2 million July, traders said.
